questions.text: What Linux command is used to display the contents of the current directory?
questions.explanation: ls with no options lists the files and subdirectories in the current directory. pwd prints the directory's path, cat prints a file's contents, and ln creates links.

questions.text: What command is used to rename a file in a Linux system?
questions.explanation: mv moves a file, and moving it to a new name in the same directory is how Linux renames. cp and dd make copies, and rm deletes.

questions.text: A system administrator of a Linux server is searching the passwd file for the username taylor that appears at the beginning of the line. Which grep command should the administrator use?
questions.explanation: ^ anchors the pattern to the start of the line, so '^taylor' only matches lines that begin with taylor. Without it, taylor could match anywhere on the line; . means any single character, and [taylor] matches any one of those letters.

questions.text: A user issues the apt-get upgrade command to update system files in an Ubuntu Linux system and receives an error message of "permission denied." What should the user do to complete the task?
questions.explanation: Upgrading packages changes system files, so it needs administrative rights. Prefixing the same command with sudo runs it with those rights. The other options either change the command or aren't real commands.
